answer_1.quote: In information retrieval (IR), fine-tuning neural retrieval models has been effective, where an encoder learns to project each document d to a dense vector close to that of a relevant query q. For domains without (q, d) pairs available for fine-tuning, pseudo-query generation (PQG), such as GPL, has been proposed, where a pseudo-query q for d is generated using large language models (LLMs)...

answer_2.quote: We employed nDCG@10 (Järvelin and Kekäläinen, 2002) as the evaluation metric, following conventions, which is widely accepted for assessing the quality of the top-10 retrieved documents.

answer_3.quote: We leverage the LLM to verify them, by prompting it to filter keywords that are relevant to d and q.
